pod.statement: The Allies lose the Second World War: Britain is forced out after the fall of France in 1940 and the Axis powers dictate the peace.
pod.baselineContext: In the attested record of 1940, Europe stood at a hinge: thrones, levies, and alliances were being renegotiated by force and marriage alike. The divergence bends the Second World War. The divergence departs from that settled course.

eras.title: The News Travels
eras.summary: The world does not change so much as re-file itself: what was certain becomes pending, and clerks inherit the first draft of the new history.
eras.detail:
The world does not change so much as re-file itself: what was certain becomes pending, and clerks inherit the first draft of the new history. The span from 1940 to 1942 reads, in retrospect, as one argument conducted in many registers: what would the ordinary strains of a changed world be allowed to cost, and who would pay it.

The record answers through its events. The succession holds (1940); The war cabinet secretariat convenes over the changed course (Later that year, 1940); Petrol prices shift in the London markets (Spring 1941). Each was a partial discharge of the same accumulated pressure, none a settlement. Contemporaries disagreed about what had happened well before they disagreed about what it meant.

By 1942 the question had not been answered so much as re-priced. What the era settled, it settled in habits and ledgers rather than treaties; what it left loaded, the next era would inherit with interest.

events.title: The succession holds
events.summary: The Allies lose the Second World War: Britain is forced out after the fall of France in 1940 and the Axis powers dictate the peace. London takes the news the way ports take weather: schedules shift before opinions do, and the harbormaster knows before the council does.

deltas.note: The immediate shock is absorbed; the accounting begins.

plausibility.rationale: Direct restatement of the divergence itself; the least contingent claim in the timeline.

events.title: The war cabinet secretariat convenes over the changed course
events.summary: The war cabinet secretariat meets in extraordinary session. Dr. Lene Aldinger argues that the moment must be committed to record before rumor rewrites it; a survey of holdings, obligations, and precedents is ordered.

deltas.note: The institution claims the divergence as its business.
Responsibility, and visibility, attach to the one who asked for the record.

plausibility.rationale: Institutions reliably respond to discontinuity with procedure; the specific convenor is the contingent part.

events.title: Petrol prices shift in the London markets
events.summary: The first measurable consequence arrives where it always does: in prices. Petrol moves against last season's rate in London, and porters, brokers, and household stewards adjust before any council does.

deltas.note: The exchequer notices what the market already knew.

plausibility.rationale: Price adjustment is the most reliable early transmission channel of any structural change.

events.title: The German Reich recalculates
events.summary: the German Reich greets the news with practiced calm and private arithmetic: garrison rosters are recounted, grain contracts re-read, and an heirloom map quietly redrawn.

deltas.note: The rival’s settled policy quietly goes back to committee.

plausibility.rationale: Neighbors always reprice risk after a discontinuity; the two-year lag matches the speed of credible intelligence.

events.title: The markets reprice around the United Kingdom
events.summary: The hinterland feeding The German Reich has fewer hands than mouths in the capital assume. Brokers adjust before any edict: contracts shorten, surety costs rise, and household stewards change what they store.

deltas.note: The market hedges; kitchens follow.

plausibility.rationale: Price adjustment is the most reliable transmission channel of structural pressure.

events.summary: What the war cabinet secretariat kept close now travels with journeymen. Rivals of The German Reich are re-equipping faster than its own arsenals admit.

deltas.note: Knowledge proves cheaper to hire than to guard.
A new name starts appearing in the registers.

plausibility.rationale: Techniques diffuse along wage gradients; guarding them raises the wage.

events.title: The war cabinet secretariat revises what the young are taught
events.summary: Over the following season the old arrangement gives way. A new syllabus fixes the changed world into schoolroom fact. The story The German Reich tells about itself has not been updated for the new circumstances; someone will update it first. Children now learn as ordinary what their grandparents called impossible.

deltas.note: The syllabus quietly rewrites what counts as common knowledge.

plausibility.rationale: Institutions metabolize discontinuity into curriculum within a generation. Revised after review: the mechanism is now named instead of asserted.

events.summary: The German Reich is drawing down forests and channels faster than they renew. A probe at the margin (an envoy recalled, a toll raised, a garrison reinforced) measures how much the world has actually changed.

deltas.note: The rival prices the new equilibrium in small provocations.

plausibility.rationale: Neighbors test any settlement whose guarantors look distracted.

artifacts.title: Letter of the broadcaster Hugh Carden on the war cabinet secretariat convenes over the changed course

paragraphs: You will have heard some version of it by now, so let me give you the true one before rumor improves it further. The war cabinet secretariat meets in extraordinary session. Dr. Lene Aldinger argues that the moment must be committed to record before rumor rewrites it; a survey of holdings, obligations, and precedents is ordered.

What it means for us: the petrol contracts must be re-sworn, and I would not extend credit past the season until we see how the war cabinet secretariat settles. Aunt Zoe asks after your health and whether the northern road is safe; I have told her yes to the first and lied about the second.
Send word by the first reliable carrier. And send the account-book. The real one.
body.postscript: P.S. The price of candles has doubled. Draw your own conclusions about how late the council is sitting.

Those closest to the affair counsel patience; those furthest from it, as usual, counsel everything else. The war cabinet secretariat is said to be preparing an accounting, which is what it is always said to be preparing.

courtRecords.advocate: The advocate submits that "Dr. Lene Aldinger attempts the grand reconciliation" stands within the record given: its cited causes are live in the world-state, its scale is modest for the era, and the objection mistakes an unfamiliar outcome for an unearned one. Histories of this dial are permitted to surprise; they are not permitted to float, and this event does not float.
courtRecords.skeptic: The skeptic answers that "Dr. Lene Aldinger attempts the grand reconciliation" asks its causes to carry more than they weigh: the cited chain establishes opportunity, not outcome, and the world-state shows no actor with both the means and the appetite. Absent an intermediate step, the event is an assertion wearing a date.

interpretations.gloss: Read the accounts and "The German Reich tests the new balance" stops being a decision at all. The money had already moved; what the chronicles record as a choice is the moment somebody finally wrote down an arrangement that had been operating for two seasons. Our rivals want a villain here. We have a ledger, and the ledger balances.

"The German Reich tests the new balance" happened because three people in one room preferred it to the alternative in front of them, and the alternative in front of them was not the one posterity imagines. The Ledger School will tell you the money decided. The money was available for either course. Somebody chose.
